xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5463: Computer use on macOS: port Orca's Swift helper with Accessibility and Screen Recording setup

plan.title: Computer use on macOS: port Orca's Swift helper with Accessibility and Screen Recording setup
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The helper (native/, scripts/, workflows) is unusable without the darwin provider (src/lib) and the provider cannot be verified without the helper; the operator already split computer use into PAN-5461/5462/5463 by platform. The DAG keeps the independent native/CI slices parallel with the gated TypeScript slices.

narratives.Problem: pan computer and Settings → Computer Use work only on Linux. Overdeck runs natively on macOS (npx @overdeck/core and the desktop app), but macOS needs a signed .app helper that holds Accessibility and Screen Recording grants, which no app can grant itself.
narratives.Proposal: Vendor Orca's MIT Swift helper into native/computer-use-macos/, adapt its trust (token + same uid), lifetime (idle exit, reconnects) and strings, build it as 'Overdeck Computer Use.app' in CI and ship the zip in the npm tarball. A darwin provider on PAN-5461's seam installs the helper to ~/.overdeck/computer-use/macos/, launches it through LaunchServices as a shared daemon on /tmp/overdeck-cu-<uid>/agent.sock, maps Linux-shape operations to the helper protocol, and walks the operator through the two permission panes from Settings. Native/CI items run before PAN-5461 merges; everything touching the seam waits behind seam-gate.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Creating or recreating any part of PAN-5461's seam: platform.ts, providers/linux.ts, routes/computer-use.ts, ComputerUseSection.tsx, tryWithDesktopLock, or the platform parameter of assertKeyComboAllowed
- Changing the ComputerUseProvider interface in platform.ts
- Buying or creating an Apple Developer ID certificate, or adding repository secrets
- Windows/WSL support (PAN-5462) and the Linux Settings page (PAN-5461)
- Orca's drag-assistant window and TCC permission reset (tccutil)
- Changing the helper's wire protocol beyond D-3/D-5/D-8/D-14
- Putting the socket under os.tmpdir() or ~/.overdeck
- Bundling the helper only in the desktop app
- A nested .gitignore under native/computer-use-macos/
- New route-scopes.ts rows

autoDecisions.summary: Planned from the PRD corrected on main in 3f991307412 and added D-14..D-20 plus an exact response-mapping table after reading the Swift source
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator directed planning from that version; the original WI-3 passthrough mapping would have broken element resolution (elementRecord needs elements[]) and JSON rendering.

autoDecisions.summary: Encode the PAN-5461 dependency as a seam-gate item that blocks every WI-3/WI-5/WI-6 item and WI-4 part B
autoDecisions.rationale: task_block cannot run before finalize creates the task state; a gate item makes the check mechanical for the work agent, matching the PRD's order paragraph.

autoDecisions.summary: Widen ComputerUseErrorCode with permission_denied only; other helper codes surface as helper_error with a code prefix
autoDecisions.rationale: permission_denied is the only helper error an operator must act on; keeping the union small avoids churn in the CLI exit-code mapping.

autoDecisions.summary: Run the macOS workflow on pushes to feature/** so Swift changes are verified before a PR exists
autoDecisions.rationale: The work agent's host is Linux and cannot run swift.

autoDecisions.summary: CI permission assertions are tolerant (log values; accept ok or permission_denied)
autoDecisions.rationale: GitHub macOS runners may pre-grant TCC permissions, so asserting not-granted could fail spuriously.

autoDecisions.summary: Set sizeJustification instead of splitting further
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue is already the macOS slice of an operator-made three-way split; the helper and provider are only verifiable together.

narrative.Action: Independent of PAN-5461. WI-1 step 1 of the PRD. Copy every file under ~/Projects/orca/native/computer-use-macos/ (Package.swift, Sources/OrcaComputerUseMacOS/main.swift, the 21 Sources/OrcaComputerUseMacOSCore/*.swift files, the 7 Tests/OrcaComputerUseMacOSTests/*.swift files) from Orca commit c6b9ac9549b (`git -C ~/Projects/orca show c6b9ac9549b:<path>`) into native/computer-use-macos/ unchanged. Add the two port-header lines (`// Ported from Orca (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Lovecast Inc.)` and `// upstream: <path> @ c6b9ac9549b`) at the top of every file; in Package.swift keep `// swift-tools-version: 6.0` as line 1 and put the headers on lines 2-3 (D-12). Add one scripts/upstream-ports.json record per file (upstream orca, path = Orca path, commit c6b9ac9549b), matching the existing native/computer-use-linux record's shape. In Package.swift rename only the executable product to `overdeck-computer-use-macos` (keep target names) and add the third header line `// modified for Overdeck: executable product renamed`. Create native/computer-use-macos/README.md modeled on native/computer-use-linux/README.md: provenance (Orca MIT, commit), a 'Modifications' list (start with the product rename), build (`npm run build:computer-macos`) and test (`swift test --package-path native/computer-use-macos`) commands, and how to re-vendor. Swift cannot compile on the Linux host; compile proof comes from wi4-ci-workflow.
